the NO chemiluminescent O3 monitor is the most accurate and reliable method for measuring O3 in wildlands fires and the NOx chemical scrubber UV O3 photometric monitor is the second most reliable and accurate.

The main takeaway from our work is that

O3 measurements in wildland fire studies and ambient air monitoring sites impacted by wildland smoke must be conducted using instruments and methodologies that are robust to the presence of VOCs and that are not susceptible to positive artifacts from VOCs.
the FRM NO chemiluminescent O3 monitors are the preferred instrument for accurate O3 measurements in wildland fire studies and at regulatory sites frequently impacted by biomass burning.
the UV photometric Ozone Monitor using a catalytic scrubber and no Nafion® dryer should not be used to measure O3 in biomass burning plumes.
